run.title: Product Research: sample report
assumptions: Ad counts only include ads that use the exact product words
Green on a map means we found nobody else selling it there, not that nobody does

headline: One brand has made this pay with ads for ten months. Copies exist from A$18, but a shopper searching Amazon or Google does not find them: none is in the top results and the best has 14 reviews. Not unique, so win on audience, not on product.

products.name: Climber's Finger Trainer (GripX Pro)
products.one_liner: One brand has made this pay with ads for ten months. Copies exist from A$18, but a shopper searching Amazon or Google does not find them: none is in the top results and the best has 14 reviews. Not unique, so win on audience, not on product.
why: Go Crimp has kept ads live since November 2025 and now runs most of the live ads for it. Nobody pays that long for ads that lose money
The copies are hidden: in both countries none shows up when a shopper types the product words into Amazon or Google, and the best-known one has 14 reviews
A supplier clearly exists (the same device retails at A$18), so the margin at US$59 is large
products.risk: The copies are hidden today, not gone. If the product takes off they will surface, and Go Crimp already owns the climbers.
next: Start in the US or Australia
Take it to an audience Go Crimp ignores: guitarists, golfers or hand rehab. 3 short ads, US$20 a day for 5 days
products.best_region: Both are light green: copies exist but shoppers do not find them.

products.advertiser_takeaway: Go Crimp owns this. 95 of the 127 live ads are theirs, and the 'other' advertisers all link to gocrimp.com, so they are Go Crimp's own creator pages. Their oldest live ad is from November 2025: ten months of proof that the ads pay.
